cases.description: Basic unused functions, classes, imports, and module variables should be found while referenced symbols stay alive.
FastAPI route handlers and dependency providers are framework entrypoints, not dead code.
Handlers registered through an explicit local registry should stay alive while unregistered handlers are reported.
Locally defined decorators that register and return functions should keep decorated entrypoints alive while unregistered helpers are still reported.
Python explicit same-name aliases are public re-export signals and should not be reported as unused imports.
Annotation metadata should bind to imported decorators even when a function parameter has the same leaf name.
A realistic model module should report only the unreferenced SQLAlchemy model while keeping used models and ORM columns quiet.
Flask blueprint routes and app CLI commands are entrypoints, while nearby unregistered helpers remain dead code.
A small service/repository package should resolve cross-file references and still find stale local strategy code.
Django management command classes and lifecycle methods are CLI entrypoints while unrelated helpers remain dead code.
Celery task decorators should keep worker functions alive while unregistered helpers are reported.
Pytest tests and fixtures are runtime entrypoints even when referenced through parameter injection.
Pydantic validators are framework-called methods while unrelated helpers are still reportable.
Alembic migration lifecycle functions and revision metadata are entrypoints; helper code can still be dead.
String-based importlib plugin loading should keep loaded plugin hooks alive while stale plugin code is reported.
pyproject project.scripts entrypoints should keep CLI functions alive.
A native Robot library decorator applied as a function retains its keyword and leaves an unregistered helper unused.
Robot variable expressions call the exact exported object method while unused helpers and another object remain reported.
Escaped Robot variable text, comments and a constant-false branch do not call an exported object method.
A package consumer reads the exact wildcard-exported import binding without retaining an unrelated import of the same module.
A reachable caller selects a literal callback name through globals without retaining an unselected callback.
An inherited receiver dispatches through a finite tuple-valued method registry and leaves unrelated or unselected methods unused.
A module variable nobody imports is unused even when other modules bind and read their own variable of the same name; imports, star imports, module attribute reads and namespace reads keep theirs.

Methods of an escaped instance that nothing in the project names are unused; literal and prefix lookups, names held as data, proxies, callbacks, protocol members, sibling implementations and instances handed outside the project keep theirs.

An unread parameter of a private function that is defined once and only called directly is unused; callbacks, partials, variadics, public functions, string lookups, constant-return default hooks, alternative definitions, abstract implementations and overridden hooks keep theirs.
Method names a class builds as strings inside a method and a dispatcher calls through getattr(channel, name) stay alive; an unlisted sibling is reported.
Callbacks registered through a source-owned decorator factory are alive regardless of the factory's method name; a factory that does not store its argument registers nothing.
